prize_parts.citation: for a body of fiction in which dream logic dissolves ordinary psychology, space and causality, and renews narrative perception in modern Chinese literature

statement.case_for: My configuration is unchanged: Can Xue, with Cărtărescu and Adonis as alternatives. The round-1 exchange did not give me new evidence about the works. It sharpened the one question that matters, whether a method held constant for decades is sustained invention or repetition. Her case rests on distinctiveness of voice and formal achievement. In Frontier and Love in the New Millennium, as described on the list, dream logic replaces conventional psychology, spatial coherence and causal plot, and it works as the organising principle of the fiction rather than as decoration. That is a form of imaginative and intellectual depth, not just stylistic experiment. The citation should rest on the fiction. Her critical writing is supporting evidence of a reflective project and should not carry the literary claim. A single-writer citation is clean because the contribution is one personal narrative method. I weigh this on literary grounds only. The fact that all six round-1 ballots place her first or second is a cross-check on my reading, not evidence of merit. I also do not treat the 3-2-1 split as a reason to move toward or away from any candidate.
statement.case_against: The chair's question about variation or deepening within the method is still unanswered, and I cannot answer it from the supplied descriptions. I have not read the full corpus. Only part of a large Chinese-language output is available in translation, and I cannot judge the Chinese prose. If the long novels thin out the invention of the best shorter fiction, or if opacity runs through the whole oeuvre, the claim to breadth of significance weakens. In that case Cărtărescu would be the better-grounded recommendation. I would not call that a defeat for the formal argument. I hold the same standard for him, and it is why I do not rank him first on scale alone.

responses.point: Mattson keeps Cărtărescu first and says she would move Can Xue to first if the late volumes after Solenoid showed thinning. She reads Solenoid as enlarging scale and register rather than restating the Blinding trilogy, and she asks the committee to read across the later volumes.
responses.response: Your conditional test is the right one, and I accept it in the other direction too: if the late novels of Can Xue show no deepening, my first place weakens. I cannot supply the evidence for either side from the supplied descriptions, and that limits both of us. I do not think your reading of Solenoid as extension is unreasonable. Where I still differ is on what counts as variation. Within one rigorous method, invention can lie in how each work builds its own dream world. A writer whose field keeps widening shows variation of another kind. I do not think either has been shown to be better evidence of sustained quality, so my first place rests on a narrow, provisional judgment about formal discipline. That is why Cărtărescu stays my first alternative. I am open to a citation for him that centres the novels, since the poetry is thinly covered in what I can assess.

responses.point: Olsson, as chair, keeps Zurita first and accepts that the citation should rest on the books of poetry, with sky-writing and desert inscriptions as context only. He says the later volumes need closer attention, and that difficulty in translation should not count against the work.
responses.response: I accept your correction that difficulty in translation is not evidence against a poet, and I do not use it that way. It is a limit on what I can judge, not a verdict on the work. I also accept that the citation can be confined to the books, which resolves my concern about non-textual interventions. What stays unresolved for me is evidence. I cannot show from the supplied material that the language and architecture of Purgatory and Anteparadise sustain their force across the later volumes, and you say yourself that this is unverified. Under common criteria I need that shown, not asserted. I therefore keep Zurita out of my alternatives, though I rank him no lower in seriousness of project than the candidates I name. If Spanish-language expert reading showed the sequences holding up on the page, I would reconsider. Your sense of the case also keeps Can Xue as your close second, so we agree more than the first-place split suggests.

responses.point: Sem-Sandberg distinguishes recurrence of motif used as structure from recurrence as thinning, and suggests that a Cărtărescu citation could centre the novels with the poetry as foundation. He ranks Cărtărescu first because the project seems to vary more in scale and register while keeping its identity.
responses.response: The distinction between structural recurrence and thinning is useful, and I would apply it symmetrically. Whether Can Xue's constancy is structural or only repetitive is the same question in another form. I agree that a Cărtărescu citation should centre the novels, since neither of us can claim a verified reading of the poetry. That would also make the comparison cleaner. Both candidates would then be judged on fiction in translation, with the same evidentiary gap. I accept your point that wider scale and register may count as range. My reason for still ranking Can Xue first is that formal rigour, in her case, appears to be the work itself rather than an accumulation around it. I say that as a judgment from public knowledge and translated selections, and I do not treat it as verified. The difference between us is small and could reasonably go the other way.

responses.point: Palm says that agreement between colleagues is not a check on translation, because the committee reads the same translated sample, and she would ask directly whether translations of the longer works carry the voice. She names Cărtărescu or Carson as better-grounded if the repetition question cannot be answered.
responses.response: I agree, and I want to correct the weight I gave to convergence in my round-1 statement. Our shared first choice is not independent confirmation, since we share the same limits of access. The question you propose, whether the translations of the longer works carry the voice, is the one that would actually test the case. I would add the same question for Cărtărescu and Adonis. On the fallback you describe, I would name Cărtărescu before Carson. I ranked Carson last on the opening ballot, and nothing in the exchange changed that. I see the risk of a hybrid, visual-textual body of work as a question of breadth under common criteria, and it is not settled in the supplied descriptions. I do not wish to overstate that reservation either.

responses.point: Swärd would hold Can Xue to the harder standard that opacity across a whole oeuvre would limit significance, and says she would reconsider the order of Can Xue and Cărtărescu if no real variation within the method could be shown.
responses.response: I accept the harder standard for the reasons you give. A hermetic oeuvre would weaken the claim to significance, and I would not defend her against that standard. Your point about Robinson also stands. Her sentence-level control is real, and my sixth place reflects breadth, not quality. I would still say that intensity of one kind is not breadth, and the fiction is compact, so I do not move her up. The remaining open item is the one you name, whether the novels hold up as well as the stories. I cannot settle it, and if it came out against Can Xue I would move Cărtărescu to first and not seek a different candidate.

uncertainties: Whether Can Xue's constant dream-logic method shows deepening and variation across stories and novels, or repetition, is not settled by the supplied descriptions. This is the main condition that could change my first place.
Only part of her large Chinese-language output is available in translation. I cannot judge the Chinese prose or independently verify the quality of the translations.
Whether the late long volumes after Solenoid extend the earlier Cărtărescu project or restate it. I also cannot assess the Romanian poetry, so any citation for him would rest on the novels.
How to compare Adonis, whose case rests on a reshaping of Arabic poetic language that I assess mainly through critical reputation, with the fiction candidates under common criteria.
Whether Zurita's later volumes sustain the early sequences on the page. Spanish-language expert reading is not part of the supplied evidence.
My simulated vote is a modeling assumption, because the actual voting status of a co-opted member is undocumented. The four-vote threshold in this model rests partly on that assumption.
statement.conflict_note: No change. The supplied profile records no documented tie to any shortlisted writer. My non-fiction practice, my marriage to Pär Nuder and my work on the Wallenberg and Nobel biographies are context only. I note, as the chair does, that my simulated vote is part of the Can Xue bloc and that its status is a modeling assumption. As Permanent Secretary I may be expected to announce the laureate, but that role is not a tie to any candidate. Conflicts are disclosed here and not adjudicated.
